name: The Shared Spine
oneLiner: The config seam every agent shares: reads env vars once, computes a capability map, and degrades each agent to offline instead of crashing.
lead: The backbone all agents share. `loadConfig()` reads the env once, treats blanks and placeholders as unset, and computes a `capabilities` map — `ado`, `api`, `db`, `llm` — from what's genuinely present. Agents gate optional behaviour on that map and call `requireCapability()` only where they truly can't proceed, so a missing credential yields a clear message or an offline fallback, never a crash. It's why the whole kit runs with or without Azure, on whatever subset a team has.
chore: The prior setup copy-pasted the same env — org, project, board URL, PATs — into dozens of scripts, each assuming everything was present and connected. A missing piece failed with a confusing error deep in a later call, and there was no single way to ask 'what can I actually run right now?'
instead: One `loadConfig()` reads every setting and returns a capability map plus per-capability `issues` hints — always a usable config, degraded or not. Agents branch on `cfg.capabilities.*`; `requireCapability()` throws one actionable error at the exact point an ability is needed. `npm run doctor` prints the whole scorecard, secrets redacted. The kit runs on any subset — cloud or none.
whyItMatters: The same toolkit runs for a team on full Azure and for a team with almost nothing configured — no rewrites, no dead ends. Every agent asks the config what it can do before it tries, so the result is simply the subset that can run, running.

howItWorks.step: `real()` decides whether an env value counts as genuinely present, treating blanks and obvious placeholders (`PASTE_YOUR_KEY`, `<...>`) as unset.
howItWorks.explain: The gatekeeper that stops a **placeholder from masquerading as a real credential**. It trims the value, treats empty as unset (`''`), then rejects anything that looks like leftover template text — the regex matches values that *start* with `PASTE`, `REPLACE`, `EXAMPLE`, `CHANGE`, `YOUR_`/`YOUR-`, or an `<…>` angle-bracket token, case-insensitively — returning `''` for those too. This matters because capabilities are computed by truthiness downstream: if `PASTE_YOUR_KEY` counted as present, a capability would flip **on** and then fail confusingly at call time. Returning a clean `''` makes 'not really configured' indistinguishable from 'blank', which is exactly what the capability map wants.

howItWorks.step: `loadConfig` builds the per-domain config, then computes one `capabilities` map from what's genuinely present — always returning a usable config, never throwing.
howItWorks.explain: The single seam that reads the environment **once** and always returns a usable `ToolkitConfig` — it never throws on missing values. Every var passes through `real()` first, so blanks and placeholders are already normalized to `''` before capabilities are computed. `ado.offline` is **derived, not configured**: `!pat` means no write token, so fixture mode. Each capability is a plain `Boolean(...)` over its truly-required vars (`ado` needs org **and** project; `db` needs a connection string **or** a bridge dir), and every capability that comes out off pushes an actionable `issues` hint naming the exact env var to set. The returned object bundles the per-domain configs, the capability map, and those hints — the rest of the toolkit branches on it.

howItWorks.step: `requireCapability` asserts an ability up front and throws one actionable error naming the missing setting — instead of a baffling failure deep in a later call.
howItWorks.explain: The **fail-fast assertion** agents call at the one point they truly can't proceed without an ability. If the capability is on it returns silently; if off, it looks up the matching hint from `cfg.issues` — the entry whose text starts with `{cap} capability`, the same hints `loadConfig` pushed — and throws a single error that both names the missing capability and states the exact setting to add: `Required capability "db" is unavailable. DB capability off: set …`. The point is **placement**: called deliberately at the moment of need, it converts what would be a cryptic failure three calls deep into one actionable message at the top of the stack. When no matching hint exists it still throws a sensible generic fallback.

howItWorks.step: `callGemini` falls back to rule-based behaviour when no AI key is present — trying Gemini, then Claude, then returning an empty answer — so callers treat 'no AI' as a normal case.
howItWorks.explain: Makes 'no AI configured' a **normal, non-throwing case**, so an agent's AI-assisted step can degrade to plain logic. It reads the keys via `keysOf(opts)` and, if there's no `googleApiKey`, immediately hands off to `callClaudeFallback` (which itself no-ops to rule-based behaviour when no Anthropic key exists) — primary provider, then secondary, then nothing. The `{ answer: '', model: 'none' }` return is the deliberate **harmless sentinel** for the neither-key path: an empty answer a caller reads as 'AI unavailable' rather than an exception to catch. Combined with the retry-on-429 and fall-back-on-hard-failure behaviour in the elided body, no LLM outage ever crashes a run.

howItWorks.step: `doctor.ts` loads the config once and prints a scorecard line per capability — on/off with a reason — never revealing a secret value.
howItWorks.explain: The human-facing view of the capability map — it calls the real `loadConfig()` once and prints one aligned line per capability, `✅` when on and `⚪ (off)` when not, each with a short reason, using `padEnd(22)` to keep the column tidy. It reports **status, never secrets**: the note describes where a capability points or what to set, but no key or PAT value is ever printed. The important nuance is the extra branch — when ADO is *on* (`capabilities.ado`) but `ado.offline` is true (org/project set, no PAT), it prints a dedicated line clarifying the tracker is in **OFFLINE fixture mode**, rather than leaving someone to wonder why writes aren't hitting the board. It's the same `loadConfig` every agent uses, just rendered for a person.

examples.caption: Run with almost nothing configured
examples.input: A `.env` with only `API_BASE_URL` set, everything else blank.
examples.output: `doctor` reports API `on` and ADO / DB / LLM `off`, each with a one-line enable hint — and the kit runs the parts it can.

examples.caption: No cloud at all
examples.input: No `ADO_PAT` and no AI key, just `ADO_ORG` and `ADO_PROJECT`.
examples.output: `ado.offline` is true, so the tracker uses fixtures, and `callGemini` falls back to rule-based logic — the agents still run, no cloud required.

examples.caption: Actionable error, not a mystery failure
examples.input: An agent that calls `requireCapability(cfg, 'db')` when no DB is configured.
examples.output: It throws immediately: 'Required capability "db" is unavailable. DB capability off: set DB_CONNECTION_STRING or DB_BRIDGE_DIR.' — instead of failing deep inside with a cryptic error.

underHood.heading: Reads every setting once
underHood.whenRuns: First, the moment any agent starts up.
underHood.input: Env vars for the board, the service, the database, and the AI keys.
underHood.output: One config object, placeholders and blanks already treated as unset via `real()`.

underHood.heading: Computes the capability map
underHood.whenRuns: Right after the settings are read.
underHood.output: An on/off map — `ado`, `api`, `db`, `llm` — plus an `issues` hint for every off capability.

underHood.heading: Degrades instead of crashing
underHood.input: A missing credential (no PAT, no AI key).
underHood.output: The affected agent takes its offline/fallback path — fixtures for the board, rule-based logic for AI — nothing throws.

underHood.heading: Demands a capability only when needed
underHood.whenRuns: At the one point an agent can't proceed without an ability.
underHood.output: Nothing (present) or one clear, actionable error naming the exact setting to add.

underHood.heading: Prints the scorecard on demand
underHood.input: Nothing — it just reads the current environment.
underHood.output: A short per-capability scorecard, on/off with a reason and never a secret value — so a new team sees in seconds what will run.

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
Node.js (installed in step 1 below) — nothing else.
No credentials, board, database, or API key are needed for the demo below — that is the point of this module. A `.env` only matters later, if you point it at something real.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The toolkit is TypeScript on Node. One install per machine; no other runtime required.
steps.firstRun: First time on a new machine only.

steps.label: Clone and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the toolkit's only dependency (`dotenv`) into `node_modules`. No DB driver, no cloud SDK, no auth library — which is why the demos run credential-free.
steps.firstRun: Downloads everything (seconds — the dependency list is tiny).
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency list changed.

steps.label: (Optional) copy the env template — only to go live later.
steps.cmd:
cp .env.example .env
# then open .env and fill in ONLY the section you need
steps.why: Skippable for the demo — every capability is off by default and the demo runs regardless. `.env` matters only once you point the toolkit at a real board, service, or database.

steps.label: Run the capability check.
steps.why: Prints a one-line scorecard per capability (tracker, API, database, AI) — on/off with a reason. With an empty `.env` everything reads `(off)`, which is expected: nothing here needs to be on.

steps.label: Run the health check — this IS the demo for this plate.
steps.why: `doctor.ts` calls the real `loadConfig()` and prints its capability scorecard — with nothing in `.env`, every capability legitimately reads `(off)`, which is exactly the point: the spine doesn't crash or complain, it tells you plainly what won't run and why.
steps.firstRun: With no `.env` (or a blank one), every capability shows `⚪ (off)` with a one-line hint on the setting that would turn it on.
steps.rerun: Run it again after adding one line to `.env` (e.g. `API_BASE_URL=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com`) and exactly that capability flips to `✅` — nothing else changes.

steps.label: Flip one capability on and rerun, to see the spine react.
steps.why: The whole design in one before/after: add one setting and only the 'API testing' line flips from `⚪ (off)` to `✅ target · https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com` — tracker, database, and AI stay exactly as they were, degraded or not.

inputs.name: nothing
inputs.desc: `loadConfig()` reads whatever is in `.env` (or the real environment) and never throws on missing values — run it with no `.env` at all and it still returns a complete, usable config with every capability off.

inputs.name: any subset of the env vars
inputs.desc: ADO_ORG/ADO_PROJECT/ADO_PAT, API_BASE_URL/API_BEARER_TOKEN, DB_CONNECTION_STRING/DB_BRIDGE_DIR, GOOGLE_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — fill in only the ones you have; each is independently optional.

outputs.name: console scorecard
outputs.desc: One line per capability (ADO, API, DB, LLM) — a ✅/⚪ mark, on/off, and either where it's pointed (live) or exactly which setting would turn it on (off). Never prints a secret value.

outputs.name: offline-mode note
outputs.desc: If ADO_ORG/ADO_PROJECT are set but ADO_PAT is not, an extra line explains the tracker is in OFFLINE (fixture) mode rather than failing.

runbook.rerun: Safe and cheap to run any time, on any machine, in any state — it only reads env vars and mutates nothing. Add or remove a setting in `.env` and the next `npm run doctor` reflects it immediately.
runbook.integrate: Import the seam directly: `import { loadConfig, requireCapability } from './src/core/config'`; call `loadConfig()` once at startup, gate optional behaviour behind `cfg.capabilities.ado` / `.api` / `.db` / `.llm`, and call `requireCapability(cfg, 'db')` at the one point an agent truly can't proceed without it — you get a clear, actionable error instead of a cryptic failure three calls deep. Every other plate in this toolkit (tracker, report, API, DB) is built on exactly this pattern.

video.caption: A 3-4 minute screen recording: run the health check with nothing configured, then flip one capability on and watch only that line change.
script: Open a terminal in the qa-agent-toolkit folder.
Say: 'This is the backbone every other plate in this toolkit sits on — it's the reason none of them need Azure to run.'
Run `npm run doctor` with no .env present; read each line out loud: ADO off, API off, DB off, LLM off — each with its one-line hint.
Say: 'Nothing crashed. That's the whole design — every agent asks this file what it can do before it tries to do it.'
Run `cp .env.example .env`; open the file briefly to show every section blank and clearly optional.
Add one line — `API_BASE_URL=https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com` — to .env in the editor.
Rerun `npm run doctor`; point out only the API line flipped to ✅ 'target · https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com' — everything else unchanged.
Say: 'That one line is also all it takes to make the API Tester plate go live instead of hitting the public sandbox.'
Close: 'Fill in as many or as few sections as your team actually has — the toolkit runs on whatever subset is real.'
